# 11. Ultimate commands

The Ultimate's drives, disk images, clock and speed.

## 11.1 Overview

#### `ULTIMATE`

U64 BBC BASIC uses the Ultimate's command interface (UCI) for files, the clock and identification, and the U64 turbo registers for speed.

```
*UVER    firmware targets
*TIME    date and time
*TURBO   CPU speed
*CAT     files (see FILES)
```

The cartridge's .cfg file switches on everything needed when the cartridge is started from the Ultimate's file browser: Command Interface, REU (16 MB), Ultimate Audio and the U64 turbo registers. Started another way, the start-up applies the same settings itself when the REU is not 16 MB or the turbo registers are off (see *SETUP).

More: *DRIVE, *MOUNT, *MENU, *REBOOT, *SAVEMEM, *CONFIG, *NET, *UPIC, *PALETTE.

#### `*STATUS` (also `*SYS`, `SYS`)

```
*STATUS     (also *SYS)
```

Shows the system: MOS and cartridge, the Ultimate's hardware, CPU speed, REU size, BASIC's memory (PAGE, TOP, LOMEM, VARTOP, HIMEM, free bytes), open files, the current directory, the drives, the network address and the clock.

#### `*UVER`

```
*UVER
```

Shows the identification of the Ultimate's DOS and control targets.

#### `*MENU` (also `*REBOOT`, `REBOOT`)

```
*MENU         the Ultimate's menu
*REBOOT [Y]   restart the C64
```

MENU opens the Ultimate's menu, as its freeze button does; the program goes on where it was when the menu is left. REBOOT restarts the C64 (and the cartridge): it asks "Reboot? (Y/N)" first unless Y is given. The program in memory is lost.

#### `*SAVEMEM`

```
*SAVEMEM file   64K of RAM to a file
```

Ultimate 64 only: saves all 64K of the C64's RAM, as it is now, to a file (overwritten if it exists), for looking at memory on a PC. A name without a leading / is in the current directory.

#### `*CONFIG` (also `*SETUP`, `SETUP`)

```
*CONFIG file   Ultimate settings
*SETUP         the settings for BASIC
```

CONFIG loads Ultimate settings from a .cfg file (the format of the Ultimate's own "Save settings": [section] lines, then item=value lines); only the items in the file change, for this session (they are not saved in the Ultimate's flash). Firmware 3.15 or later; on an SD card or USB stick put the file in a folder (/SD/cfg/my.cfg: firmware 3.15a cannot open one in the drive's root).

SETUP applies the settings this BASIC needs (the same as the u64bbc .cfg file next to the cartridge: command interface, REU of 16 MB, Ultimate Audio, the U64's turbo registers, the SIDs), then finds the REU and the turbo again. The start-up does this by itself when the REU is not 16 MB or a U64 has its turbo registers off, and says so in one line.


## 11.2 Drives and disk images

#### `*DRIVE`

```
*DRIVE A|B ON|OFF
```

Switches one of the Ultimate's drives on or off.

#### `*MOUNT`

```
*MOUNT <image> [A|B|<device>]
```

Mounts a disk image (D64, D71, D81, G64 ...) on one of the Ultimate's drives, drive A if none is given.

```
*MOUNT /USB0/games/elite.d64
*MOUNT disk2.d64 B
```

#### `*UNMOUNT`

```
*UNMOUNT [A|B|<device>]
```

Removes the disk image from a drive (drive A if none is given).

#### `*SWAP`

```
*SWAP [A|B|<device>]
```

Moves a drive (drive A if none is given) on to the next disk of its disk set, as the Ultimate's swap function does for multi-disk games.

#### `*PARTITION`

```
*PARTITION <n> <path> [<name>]
*PARTITION <n> OFF
```

Makes partition n of the Ultimate's SoftIEC drive point to a directory. From firmware 3.15 the SoftIEC drive reaches files only through partitions; without one it serves /Temp. OFF removes a partition (not effective on firmware 3.15a).

```
*PARTITION 3 /USB0/c64 GAMES
*CP 3
```

#### `*PARTITIONS`

```
*PARTITIONS
```

Lists the SoftIEC drive's partitions (its "$=P" directory).

#### `*CP`

```
*CP <n>
```

Selects partition n on the SoftIEC drive (the drive's own CP command).


## 11.3 Clock and speed

#### `*TIME`

```
*TIME
```

Prints the date and time of the Ultimate's clock. The BASIC variable TIME is a separate centisecond counter.

#### `*SETTIME`

```
*SETTIME yyyy/mm/dd hh:mm:ss
```

Sets the Ultimate's clock. The Ultimate's settings can forbid this (error "Function prohibited").

#### `*TURBO`

```
*TURBO          show the speed index
*TURBO MAX      fastest (index 15)
*TURBO OFF      1 MHz (index 0)
*TURBO <n>      speed index 0-15
```

Needs the U64 turbo registers (Turbo Control in the Ultimate's settings, switched on by the cartridge's .cfg). Index 15 is 48 MHz on an Ultimate 64 and 64 MHz on an Elite II or C64 Ultimate. See SPEED.

#### `SPEED`

On an Ultimate 64 or C64 Ultimate with the U64 turbo registers enabled, BBC BASIC starts at the highest speed of the machine: 48 MHz (Ultimate 64, Elite) or 64 MHz (Elite II, C64 Ultimate). That is 25 to 30 times a BBC Micro.

TIME stays in real time at every speed. *TURBO shows or changes the speed. On an Ultimate II+ or a plain C64 the speed is 1 MHz.
